items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: and Frankie Dunlap made one side of the record, too

ctx.x: Well, I said we did this Chicago Sound, and the next thing I knew they had a big Chicago Sound night down at Birdland. So I go there and oh boy, the place was packed -- I mean with news people, reporters; I don't know what reaction -- I don't know whether they were promoting the record or the record had been out for some time, and, we got a very favorable mention, I know that.

And Wilbur Campbell went back to Chicago, and Frankie Dunlap made one side of the record, too, because Wilbur had to leave the next month after the initial side, and Junior Mance had left, and so we used Kenny Drew down at Birdland, but it was a beautiful night, and amost every other night, I had ... Monday night I had a job down there.

And he called me up for a gig -- Mr. Stan Getz, and Elvin Jones, Wynton Elmer, Joe Kelly and myself, and we were working -- that's Red Garland, Philly Joe, Trane, Paul, and himself opposite the Miles Davis Quintet -- at Birdland.
